name: Drift
from: Customization Game: a dress-up game that keeps suggesting changes; the end shows how far you drifted from your first choices.
hook: Make the character you want. The game has a few suggestions.
pitch: A dress-up game across four categories. Every pick is met with a suggestion, politely at first, then sweeter and pushier. You never have to accept. The last screen puts what you made beside what you first chose, with the percentage that came from the game.
minute_check: Yes: the comparison screen sells it.
build_check: Yes: sixteen parts and one comparison screen.
scope: Four categories, four options each. The comparison screen is the payoff; build it early.

brief.player: A designer making a character across categories (hair, eyes, clothing).
brief.fail: None. You are never forced; the game only insists.
brief.ending: Side by side: what you made, and what you would have made without the suggestions, with a percentage of influence.
brief.verb: Pick, then accept or refuse the suggestion.
brief.theme: AI drift: small suggestions, each reasonable, add up to someone else’s idea.
brief.look: 8-bit arcade palette (after the arcade in WarGames); pop-ups that grow sweeter and pushier.

prov.bug: It says the blue jacket is 23% better. Sure!
prov.nit: Better by whose measure? Does the game ever say?

refs_lit: How small defaults steer choices without forcing them: your mechanic, in the research.
Harry Brignull, dark patterns (darkpatterns.org, 2010; now deceptive.design)
A catalogue of interfaces that push. Use it to name each pop-up style.
Interactive evolution where people steer images by choosing; a counterpoint where the human’s taste drives.
omni_gameplay_prompt: 8-bit WarGames-era neon arcade character-creator game in deep midnight plum (#1a1033), soft pastel pink (#ffe3f1), and hot arcade magenta (#ff5fa2). Steady front-on studio UI camera. On the left, an expressive pixel-art avatar swaps hair, jacket, and boots as vibrant item tiles highlight on the right; each selection triggers a bouncy, increasingly flashy magenta assistant pop-up badge nudging a shinier outfit swap until the screen splits to compare the original avatar beside the heavily restyled twin. Continuous unbroken gameplay shot, no scene cuts, no gibberish text. Use the reference image for split avatar-and-wardrobe layout and palette. Sound design: bubbly 8-bit arcade synth, cheerful pop-up bloops. No dialogue.
